Intel (INTC) Stock Dropped, So What Is Driving Attention Now?
Simply Wall St

INTC
688825.SS
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Intel (INTC) stock slipped alongside the wider chip sector as investors reacted to Chinese rival CXMT's reported progress and fresh warnings about how long AI infrastructure spending and higher interest rates can support recent valuations.

Recent news around CXMT and sector-wide AI spending concerns hit Intel's share price hard in the short term, with a 1-day share price return of down 4.56% and a 7-day share price return of down 8.37%. At the same time, the 1-year total shareholder return of 166.34% and 3-year total shareholder return of 179.68% point to strong longer term momentum that investors are now reassessing against higher rates and rich AI expectations.

See how other AI chip and data center players are reacting to the same pressures by reviewing the hand-picked 93 AI infrastructure stocks that could be next in line for sharp sentiment swings.

Intel now trades below recent highs after a sharp pullback and a record-setting run in AI driven revenue. Does that reset leave enough upside to justify the risks investors are being asked to carry here?

Most Popular Narrative: 80.4% Undervalued

Intel last closed at $98.12, while the most followed narrative pegs fair value far higher at $500.93, so the market and this framework are worlds apart on what the stock is worth.

Reasons I bought Intel:

• x86 software. a lot of existing software has been created for the x86 architecture and additionally has likely been optimized to run on intel cpus due to them having been the consistent market leader for so long giving them an advantage over AMD.

• This is most noticed when comparing applications using IBOT or Intel Compiler

See why 87 investors see Intel as 80% undervalued.

According to Suen, this valuation view rests on Intel's entrenched x86 software ecosystem and its role as a large US based foundry, with an assumed discount rate of 11.31% and a fair value that implies the shares trade at a very large discount of 80.4% to that estimate.

Result: Fair Value of $500.93 (UNDERVALUED)

However, several pressure points still hang over the Intel narrative, including CXMT's progress in China and any reset in AI infrastructure budgets that cools current enthusiasm.

Find out about the key risks to this Intel narrative.

Another View: Intel Through A Cash Flow Lens

The crowd narrative around Intel leans heavily on long term potential, yet our DCF model paints a cooler picture. On this framework, Intel at $98.12 trades above an estimated future cash flow value of $79.33. This points to the shares looking overvalued rather than deeply discounted.

What Happened?

A number of stocks fell in the morning session after hotter-than-expected inflation data compounded fears that elevated borrowing costs will curb artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

The sell-off followed a Bureau of Labor Statistics release showing September wholesale prices climbed 1.3%, marking a 6.3% annual advance that outpaced the 5.5% projection from economists polled by Dow Jones. Compounding an above-forecast consumer price print from the prior session, the hotter CPI inflation reading drove the 10-year Treasury yield past 5.27%, based on CNBC market data. However, rates cooled off a bit in the pre market session.Higher benchmark rates threaten the debt-heavy funding required to power data center expansion. Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives observed in a client note carried by CNBC that while compute demand remains sound, climbing yields directly inflate project financing costs and intensify scrutiny on balance sheets.

Semiconductor valuations reflect aggressive, uninterrupted capital spending from cloud hyperscalers. When capital costs stay elevated, the payback timeline on multi-billion-dollar clusters lengthens, raising the hurdle rate for new hardware commitments and delaying order realization across the component supply chain.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Intel's EMIB-T and TSMC's CoWoS are competing approaches to advanced packaging.

Wei said TSMC is already producing advanced packages at 5x reticle size with "excellent" yields, which has kept customers satisfied.

Wei added that the company is also working to reduce packaging costs, stating that its CoWoS technology remains customers' preferred option.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) CEO C.C. Wei hinted during the company's earnings call that the chipmaker could step in if customers struggle to secure enough advanced-packaging supply from Intel (INTC).

The remarks came after Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan asked whether TSMC would support customers that initially chose Intel's EMIB-T packaging technology but later faced supply constraints, according to the Koyfin transcript of the company's third-quarter (Q3) earnings call.

TSM stock retail sentiment on October 15 as of 10:30 a.m. ET | Source: Stocktwits
Intel Vs. TSMC

Intel's EMIB-T and TSMC's Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) are competing approaches to advanced packaging that connect chip components and high-bandwidth memory into integrated systems used in AI computing.

A shortage of packaging capacity can delay deliveries even when the underlying chips are available. Should that happen, clients can either delay their launch or switch to a different supplier.

During Intel's second-quarter (Q2) earnings call in July, CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that EMIB-T orders were growing and yield and reliability targets were being met, with the company preparing to scale production to support customers' 2027 ramps.

title: Intel vs. Qualcomm: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Intel vs. Qualcomm: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Erin Kennedy, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:57 AM PDT 6 min read
INTC
QCOM
AMAT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The semiconductor landscape is shifting as AI demands redefine hardware requirements. Choosing between Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) requires weighing a massive manufacturing turnaround against a mobile titan's expansion.

Intel is betting its future on becoming a world-class foundry for other chip designers, while Qualcomm is leveraging its 5G leadership to capture new markets in automotive and computing. Both companies are central to the technology narrative, but they offer vastly different financial profiles and risk levels for investors.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures processors, accelerators, and software, serving as a heavyweight among semiconductor stocks. It is aggressively expanding its foundry business to produce chips for other designers, recently deepening its partnership with Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT). This strategy targets the growing need for specialized hardware in a world increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence.

In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $52.9 billion, a slight decline of roughly 0.5% from the previous year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $267 million, which resulted in a net margin of negative 0.5%. This performance reflects the massive research and development costs associated with reclaiming its process technology leadership after several years of falling behind competitors.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Intel has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity. Its current ratio, comparing short-term assets to liabilities, is a healthy 2, but free cash flow was negative at nearly $4.9 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 25.1% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Qualcomm

Qualcomm develops essential wireless technologies, providing modems and processors for major smartphone brands like Samsung and Xiaomi (OTC:XIACF). It also generates significant income by licensing its massive portfolio of 5G intellectual property to other manufacturers. A high concentration of sales comes from a few massive customers like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), and customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In fiscal 2025, revenue reached roughly $44.3 billion, representing growth of nearly 13.7% from the prior year. Qualcomm achieved net income of approximately $5.5 billion, resulting in a net margin of 12.5%. This net margin indicates the percentage of total revenue that remains as profit after all expenses are paid, showing the company's ability to turn sales into actual earnings.

title: The Case For NVIDIA Stock Rests On One Thing
detail:
The Case For NVIDIA Stock Rests On One Thing
Trefis Team

NVDA
AMD
INTC
AVGO
QCOM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

NVIDIA (NVDA) has translated demand for its AI platform into rapid sales growth. NVIDIA can only sell the hardware its partners build, leaving the open risk for shareholders with component manufacturers. The company has yet to prove these suppliers can keep pace with customer appetite. This issue matters today because NVIDIA has guided to another round of higher sales for the quarter it reports next.

Management Says NVIDIA's Suppliers Are Running Flat Out

Executives have acknowledged challenges across NVIDIA's entire supply chain, noting that everyone involved is running flat out. This assessment emerged during the August 26, 2026 earnings call, when analysts questioned the company about demand and the most acute shortages. Discussions on that call included shortages in DRAM memory chips and wafer capacity at chip foundries. Analysts additionally brought up power and physical space for data centers, which sit outside the direct scope of parts NVIDIA buys.

On the demand side, executives stated their belief that most AI now operates as agents. For the time being, NVIDIA's suppliers appear to set the limit on its sales just as much as its customers do.

NVIDIA Is Counting On Even More From Its Suppliers

NVIDIA has guided to revenue of $108 billion for its fiscal 2027 third quarter. This compares to the $96.2 billion reported for the fiscal 2027 second quarter. The guide sits about $12 billion above the second quarter, and manufacturers must physically build every product necessary to hit that mark. The increase follows second-quarter sales that were already up 105.9% from a year earlier. NVIDIA therefore requires even greater output from suppliers that have already had to keep up with that growth.

NVIDIA stock trades at 27.8 times its earnings over the past twelve months, against 22.7 for the S&P 500. This price appears to assume that manufacturing partners will successfully keep pace with the sales NVIDIA has guided to.

What Has NVIDIA Said About Adding Capacity?

Management notes that additional production capacity is coming online all the time, though it will not arrive all at once. The company expects better yields, which means extracting more usable chips from each wafer. Executives also say NVIDIA will work with every one of its suppliers.

These statements outline the expected trajectory for new supply. The pace at which this new supply arrives will materialize in NVIDIA's reported sales. Measured against the $108 billion guide, the company's fiscal 2027 third-quarter revenue is the figure to watch at its next report, expected on or around November 17, 2026.
